faqs.a: The step is added to the current value repeatedly. A step of 2 from 1 gives 1, 3, 5, 7, ... A step of 0.5 gives 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, ... The step can be any non-zero number, including decimals.
faqs.q: What does the step value mean?

faqs.a: Yes. Enter a start larger than the end and a negative step. For example, start 10, end 1, step -1 gives 10, 9, 8, ..., 1.
faqs.q: Can I make a countdown list?

faqs.a: The count is floor((end - start) / step) + 1 when the step points toward the end. For start 1, end 10, step 2: (10 - 1) / 2 = 4.5, floored to 4, plus 1 = 5 numbers.
faqs.q: How many numbers will my list have?

faqs.a: Tap the download button to save the list as a plain text file (number-list.txt), one number per line. Or use the copy button to grab a comma-separated version.

faqs.a: It generates up to 5,000 numbers per run and shows a note when the range would produce more. That keeps the browser fast and the page light.
faqs.q: Is there a limit on list size?

faqs.a: No. A zero step would repeat the start forever, which is not a list. Enter a non-zero step, positive or negative.

generate-list-of-numbers.formula:
With step s > 0: start, start+s, start+2s, ... up to the last value <= end.
Count = floor((end - start) / s) + 1.
With step s < 0: values descend from start to the last value >= end.
howTo: Enter the starting number of your list.
Enter the ending number (it can be smaller than the start).
Enter the step - how much to add each time (negative steps count down).
The full list and its count appear instantly.
Copy the list or download it as a text file.
keyFacts: A number list is an arithmetic sequence: each term adds the same step to the previous one.
The step can be positive, negative, a whole number or a decimal - but never zero.
A positive step with start above end (or negative step with start below end) produces an empty list.
Count = floor((end - start) / step) + 1, which this tool computes for you.
Lists are capped at 5,000 items to protect browser performance.
The download saves one number per line, ready for Excel or code.

generate-list-of-numbers.workedExample:
Generate from 1 to 10 with step 2:
1. Start at 1.
2. Add the step: 1 + 2 = 3, then 5, 7, 9.
3. Next would be 11, which is past the end (10), so stop.
4. List: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.
5. Count = floor((10 - 1) / 2) + 1 = floor(4.5) + 1 = 5 numbers.
